# Config schema + layered-merge core + capability descriptor (provider-neutral)

## Context / Problem

The reconciler's rebar↔Jira mappings are hardcoded literals in
`adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py`, `config.py`, and `inbound_fields.py` (all under
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`). Before any axis can become config-driven, the seam
needs a provider-neutral foundation: a config schema, a layered overlay/merge, fail-closed
validation, and a capability descriptor declaring which axes a target has. This is the
walking skeleton every other child depends on; it ships with **no axis wired yet** — S2–S5
move each axis onto it.

## Approach

Add a provider-neutral module (new file
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mapping_config.py`) that:

1. **Parses** the mapping block as a **reserved config section**, not as new keys on the
   typed `JiraConfig`. The core coercer coerces `[tool.rebar.jira]` into `JiraConfig`
   (fields `url`/`user`/`project`/`allow_insecure`) and `_warn_unknown` warns — or
   hard-errors under `REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error` — on any leftover key, so mapping
   keys **cannot** hang off `[tool.rebar.jira]`. Instead add a new reserved section name
   `mapping` to `_RESERVED_SECTIONS` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:633`, today
   `{"llm", "snapshot"}`) so the parser recognises `[tool.rebar.mapping]` without coercing
   or warning, read raw via `rebar.config.read_reserved_section("mapping")`
   (`src/rebar/config.py:597`) — the exact pattern the optional `llm.*` layer uses. Shape:
   a `default` block and a `projects.<KEY>` table, each carrying axis sub-tables
   (`status_map`, `type_map`, `link_map`, `priority_map`, `create_defaults`) plus
   discovered-vocabulary lists (`statuses`, `issue_types`, `link_types`, a `hierarchy` level
   map). Absent section ⇒ empty overlay (today's behavior).
2. **Resolves** an effective mapping per project key with two merge rules (load-bearing for
   validation): (a) the **axis maps** (`status_map`/`type_map`/`link_map`/`priority_map`/
   `create_defaults`) **deep-merge per key** — built-in ← `default` ← `projects.<KEY>` — so
   an overlay entry overrides only the key it names and unnamed keys inherit; (b) the
   **vocabulary lists** (`statuses`/`issue_types`/`link_types`/`hierarchy`) **replace
   wholesale, most-specific wins** (NOT unioned): a project's declared vocabulary is
   authoritative-complete, so `projects.<KEY>.statuses` fully supersedes `default.statuses`,
   and a layer with no list inherits the next-outer one. Unioning would wrongly accept a
   value in the default but not the project. This matches `_deep_merge`'s
   wholesale-array-replace (`_config_sources.py:215`).
3. **Validates** fail-closed at load against the **effective** (resolved) vocabulary from
   rule (b): every axis-map value must appear in its declared vocabulary set when one is
   declared (e.g. every `status_map` value ∈ effective `statuses`); a value referencing a
   capability-absent axis is rejected; a **malformed block** raises — a sub-table that is
   not a mapping, an axis-map value that is not a string (nor the `skip` sentinel), or a
   vocabulary list that is not a list of strings. The raised type is a new
   `MappingConfigError` subclassing `rebar._config_coercion.ConfigError`
   (`src/rebar/_config_coercion.py:20`), failing closed on the same load path as every
   other config error. Validation is **offline** — config only, never the network.
4. Defines a **`Capability` descriptor** dataclass declaring which mapping **axes** the
   target's vocabulary has (`has_types`, `has_transitions`, `has_hierarchy`,
   `has_link_types`, `has_priorities`) — data about the target's vocabulary, distinct from
   the backend role/behaviour Protocols in `_backend.py` (`@runtime_checkable`
   `SupportsLinks`/`SupportsComments`, cc77 hasattr-narrowing), which describe which
   operations a backend object implements. Where they overlap (link support) the descriptor
   is derived from the Protocol, not a second source of truth.

The module imports nothing from the Jira adapter (provider-neutral); the adapter injects
its built-in defaults and capability values, respecting the vendor-adapter seam's one-way
dependency direction (concrete backends import the neutral core, never the reverse) —
`docs/adr/0083-reconciler-vendor-adapter-seam.md` (cite the filename; a bare "ADR 0035" is
ambiguous), amended by `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md`.

Relationship to the existing per-project surface: `.bridge_state/projects.json`
(`projects_store.py`, ADR 0097) binds a store to a Jira project **identity**;
`[tool.rebar.mapping].projects.<KEY>` declares that key's **vocabulary/semantics** —
orthogonal concerns in separate homes, joined on the same Jira key without duplicating
identity data.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — add `"mapping"` to `_RESERVED_SECTIONS`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mapping_config.py` (new) — schema dataclasses,
  `MappingConfigError`, `load_mapping_config`, `resolve_for_project`, `validate`,
  `Capability`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_mapping_config.py` (new).
- `docs/config.md` — document the `[tool.rebar.mapping]` section shape, three-layer merge,
  and orthogonality to `.bridge_state/projects.json`.

## Testing

- **Reserved-section recognition (unit, real parser):** a `[tool.rebar.mapping]` section
  is neither warned as unknown nor coerced into `JiraConfig`, and is returned raw by
  `read_reserved_section("mapping")` — even under `REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error`.
- **Merge precedence (unit):** a `projects.REB.status_map` entry wins over
  `default.status_map` over an injected built-in default, an unnamed key inherits; a
  `projects.REB.statuses` list wholesale-replaces `default.statuses` (not unioned), and a
  layer with no list inherits the outer one.
- **Config-effect contrast:** resolve at the built-in default vs a non-default overlay and
  assert the effective map differs as specified (guards read-but-miswired).
- **Fail-closed validation (failure path):** a `status_map` value outside declared
  `statuses`, a malformed block, and an axis-absent reference each raise
  `MappingConfigError`, with the nearest valid config as the negative control (must NOT
  raise).
- **Neutrality:** `mapping_config` imports no `adapters.jira*` module and contains no Jira
  value literal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `[tool.rebar.mapping]` is registered as a reserved section and read raw via
  `read_reserved_section`, so its keys do not trip `_warn_unknown` even under
  `REBAR_CONFIG_UNKNOWN_KEYS=error` — verified by
  `test_mapping_config.py::test_reserved_section_not_unknown`.
- [ ] Axis maps deep-merge per key (built-in ← default ← project; unnamed key inherits)
  while vocabulary lists replace wholesale (most-specific wins, not unioned) — verified by
  `::test_perkey_merge_precedence` and `::test_vocab_lists_replace_wholesale`.
- [ ] A non-default overlay yields a different effective mapping than the built-in default
  through the real resolve path — verified by `::test_config_effect_contrast`.
- [ ] `validate` fails closed offline with `MappingConfigError` on a value outside the
  effective vocabulary, a malformed block (non-mapping sub-table, non-string map value, or
  non-string-list vocabulary), and a capability-absent axis reference; the nearest valid
  config does not raise — verified by `::test_validate_fails_closed`.
- [ ] The core is provider-neutral: `mapping_config` imports no `adapters.jira*` module and
  carries no Jira value literal — verified by `::test_core_is_provider_neutral`.
- [ ] `docs/config.md` documents the reserved-section shape and its three-layer merge, with
  an explicit note that it is orthogonal to `.bridge_state/projects.json`.

Test tier: **in-process unit** — the mechanism is config parse/merge/validate over real
functions (the real reserved-section parser plus the new pure resolve/validate); no
external boundary is crossed, so no lower or higher tier applies.
